name: Guinea-Bissau
summary: An archipelago of eighty-eight islands with saltwater hippos, nesting turtles and a matrilineal society that still chooses its own kings — and a mainland of mangrove and rice paddy behind it.
when: November to April. Turtle nesting on Poilao peaks between July and October.

entries.caption: The Bijagos
entries.description: Eighty-eight islands, twenty of them inhabited, and a UNESCO biosphere reserve over all of it.
entries.subject: palm-fringed islands and tidal channels in the Bijagos archipelago

entries.caption: Mangrove and Tide
entries.description: The tidal range here is five metres, and the channels between the islands change with it.
entries.subject: mangrove channels at low tide in the Bijagos

entries.caption: Saltwater Hippos
entries.description: The hippos of Orango swim in the sea between islands, which almost no others do.
entries.subject: a hippo in shallow salt water off Orango island

entries.caption: Turtles at Poilao
entries.description: One of the largest green turtle nesting sites in the Atlantic, on an uninhabited island.
entries.subject: a green turtle returning to the sea at dawn on Poilao

entries.caption: Flat Country
entries.description: The highest point is three hundred metres. This is a country of water, not relief.
entries.subject: flat green rice paddy stretching to a treeline

entries.caption: None to Speak Of
entries.description: No falls — the land has nowhere to fall from. The water here moves sideways with the tide.
entries.subject: a tidal creek running through mangrove at Cacheu

entries.caption: The Geba and the Corubal
entries.description: Two rivers cutting deep estuaries into the mainland, navigable a long way up.
entries.subject: the wide brown estuary of the Geba river

entries.caption: Island Sand
entries.description: Bubaque, Rubane and Orango have empty palm-backed beaches and warm water.
entries.subject: an empty palm-backed beach on Rubane island

entries.caption: Palm and Sacred Grove
entries.description: Oil palm through the islands, and groves that are ceremonial ground and off limits.
entries.subject: oil palms and dense forest on a Bijagos island

entries.caption: Island Hopping by Pirogue
entries.description: There are no bridges. Everything is boats, tides and waiting, and that is the pleasure of it.
entries.subject: a motorised pirogue crossing between Bijagos islands

entries.caption: Matrilineal, and Still So
entries.description: Bijago women choose husbands, own the houses, and hold the religious authority.
entries.subject: Bijago women in ceremonial dress on an island beach

entries.caption: The Bijagos
entries.description: Age grades govern life, and the vaca-bruto initiation is danced in a bull mask.
entries.subject: a Bijago dancer in a carved bull mask at a village ceremony

entries.caption: Rice, Cashew and Bica
entries.description: Rice from the paddies, cashew as the whole export economy, and Portuguese coffee.
entries.subject: a plate of rice with fish and palm oil sauce

entries.caption: Carnival in Bissau
entries.description: Masks, drums and neighbourhood competition, Portuguese in form and entirely local in content.
entries.subject: masked dancers at the Bissau carnival

entries.caption: Carving and Cloth
entries.description: Bijago bull and shark masks, and the woven pano de pente cloth used as currency.
entries.subject: a carved Bijago shark mask and woven pano cloth

entries.caption: Cacheu
entries.description: A slaving fort of 1588 on the river, and one of the oldest European buildings in West Africa.
entries.subject: the old Portuguese fort and cannon at Cacheu

entries.caption: The Bijagos Biosphere
entries.description: The whole archipelago is a UNESCO biosphere reserve, run with the island communities.
entries.subject: a community ranger boat among the Bijagos islands

entries.caption: Bissau
entries.description: A small Portuguese-built capital with a decaying Bissau Velho quarter and very good music.
entries.subject: the faded Portuguese colonial buildings of Bissau Velho

entries.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Palm Thatch
entries.description: Tiled colonial fronts in Bissau, and rectangular palm-thatch houses through the islands.
entries.subject: a palm-thatched island house with a swept sand yard

entries.caption: Sunday at the Beach
entries.description: Bissau goes to Bubaque and the near islands at weekends, by ferry, with a stereo.
entries.subject: a crowded island ferry leaving Bissau on a Sunday

entries.caption: Boats and Beaches
entries.description: Not for very small children — the boats are open and the tides are serious.
entries.subject: a family on the sand beside a beached pirogue

entries.caption: Fishing the Channels
entries.description: Barracuda and tarpon in the passes between islands, on light tackle.
entries.subject: an angler casting from a boat in a Bijagos channel

entries.caption: Two or Three Lodges
entries.description: Small fishing and eco-lodges on Rubane and Orango, and not much else anywhere.
entries.subject: a small thatched eco-lodge among palms on a Bijagos island

entries.caption: Community Conservation
entries.description: The island communities police the turtle beaches themselves, and it works.
entries.subject: villagers recording a turtle nest on a Bijagos beach

entries.caption: Tide and Palm
entries.description: The channels at low water, when the mangrove roots come out and the light goes flat.
entries.subject: exposed mangrove roots and channels at low tide

entries.caption: Orango
entries.description: Hippos, an island king, and a lodge with no road on the island at all.
entries.subject: a savanna clearing with hippo tracks on Orango island

entries.caption: Why Guinea-Bissau
entries.description: Saltwater hippos, nesting turtles, and a society run by its women.
entries.subject: a pirogue crossing still water between two Bijagos islands
